**Idea.**  
Write the generating polynomial of a shifty \(\alpha\) as  

\[
A(x)=\sum_{i=0}^8\alpha(i)x^i\in\mathbb Z[x],\qquad\deg A\le8 .
\]

The condition “\(\exists\beta,k\neq l\) with \((S_n\alpha)\!\star\!\beta=1_{ \{k,l\}}\)” is equivalent to  

\[
A(x)\,G(x)=1+x^d\tag{1}
\]

for some integer \(d>0\) and some Laurent polynomial \(G(x)\in\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]\).  
Indeed \((S_n\alpha)\!\star\!\beta\) is the cross‑correlation, i.e. the product of \(A(x)\) with the reversed \(\beta\).

Since monomials are units in \(\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]\), (1) holds iff  

\[
A(x)=x^m f(x),\qquad f\mid (1+x^d)\text{ in }\mathbb Z[x],
\]

with \(m\ge0\) and \(\deg A=m+\deg f\le8\).  
All divisors of \(1+x^d\) are products of distinct cyclotomic polynomials \(\Phi_n\) with even index \(n\) (because \(\Phi_n\mid x^d+1\iff n\) is even).  

Thus  

\[
A(x)=\pm x^m\prod_{n\in S}\Phi_n(x),
\]

where \(S\) is a set of even integers, each \(\Phi_n\) appears at most once, and  

\[
\sum_{n\in S}\varphi(n)\le8-m .
\]

Only even \(n\) with \(\varphi(n)\le8\) can appear; they are  

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
n&\varphi(n)\\\hline
2&1\\4,6&2\\8,10,12&4\\14,18&6\\16,20,24,30&8
\end{array}
\]

(12 polynomials total).  

**Counting.**  
Let \(d_S=\sum_{n\in S}\varphi(n)\). For each admissible set \(S\) (i.e. \(d_S\le8\)) we may choose any shift \(m\) with \(0\le m\le8-d_S\) (giving \(9-d_S\) choices) and a sign \(\pm\) (2 choices).  

Hence the number of shifty functions is  

\[
N=2\sum_{S\subseteq\{12\text{ cyclotomics}\},\,d_S\le8}(9-d_S).
\]

Enumerating all subsets (44 of them) gives  

\[
N=2\bigl(9\cdot1+8\cdot3+7\cdot6+6\cdot10+5\cdot12+4\cdot8+3\cdot4+2\cdot0\bigr)={answer = 266}.
\]

**Pitfalls.**  
- Forgetting that monomials are units, so a factor \(x^m\) can be moved to the other side.  
- Assuming coefficients of \(\alpha\) can be arbitrary; they must be \(\pm1\) at the highest degree (product of monic cyclotomics).  
- Missing that only even‑indexed cyclotomics divide some \(x^d+1\).  

Thus exactly 266 shifty functions exist.

**Key insight** –  
For a shifty \(\alpha\) we need a \(\beta\) with  
\[
S_n(\alpha)\star\beta =\begin{cases}1&n=k,l\\0&\text{else}\end{cases}
\iff \alpha(x)\,\beta'(x)=x^k+x^l .
\]  
Thus \(\alpha\) must divide a binomial \(x^k+x^l\) in the Laurent integer ring.  
Since units are \(\pm x^m\), this is equivalent to \(\alpha\) dividing \(1+x^d\) for some \(d>0\).

**Cyclotomic factorisation** –  
\(1+x^d=\prod_{\substack{n\mid2d\\ n\nmid d}}\Phi_n(x)\).  
All such \(\Phi_n\) have even index \(n\) with the same 2‑adic valuation: if \(v_2(d)=t\) then each factor has \(v_2(n)=t+1\).  
Hence any divisor \(\alpha\) is a product of distinct cyclotomic polynomials \(\Phi_{2^{t+1}o}\) (odd \(o\)) all sharing the same \(t\).

**Degree bound** –  
\(\alpha\) is supported in \([0,8]\), so \(\deg\alpha\le8\).  
\(\deg\Phi_{2^{t+1}o}=2^{t}\varphi(o)\).  
Require \(2^{t}\varphi(o)\le8\).  
This yields possible \(t\) and odd \(o\):

| t | odd o | n=2^{t+1}o | deg |
|---|------|-----------|------|
|0|1,3,5,7,9,15|2,6,10,14,18,30|1,2,4,6,6,8|
|1|1,3,5|4,12,20|2,4,8|
|2|1,3|8,24|4,8|
|3|1|16|8|

These are the only cyclotomic factors that can appear.

**Form of \(\alpha\)** –  
\(\alpha(x)=x^{r}\,A(x)\) where \(r\ge0\), \(A\) is a product of a *subset* of the above cyclotomics **all from the same \(t\)**, and \(\deg A\le8\).  
For each such \(A\) there are \(9-\deg A\) choices of \(r\) (so that \(\deg\alpha\le8\)).  
The empty product \(A=1\) (the monomial case) contributes \(9\) functions.

**Counting subsets** –  
List cyclotomics per \(t\) and count non‑empty subsets with total degree ≤8:

- \(t=0\): 6 cyclotomics (deg 1,2,4,6,6,8) → 14 admissible subsets.  
- \(t=1\): 3 cyclotomics (deg 2,4,8) → 4 subsets.  
- \(t=2\): 2 cyclotomics (deg 4,8) → 2 subsets.  
- \(t=3\): 1 cyclotomic (deg 8) → 1 subset.

**Total shifty functions**  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\# &=9\;(\text{A}=1)\\
&\quad+\sum_{\text{subsets}}(9-\deg A)\\
&=9+\bigl[14\cdot9-\!\!\sum_{\text{subsets }t=0}\deg A\bigr]
   +\bigl[4\cdot9-\!\!\sum_{\text{subsets }t=1}\deg A\bigr]\\
&\qquad +\bigl[2\cdot9-\!\!\sum_{\text{subsets }t=2}\deg A\bigr]
   +\bigl[1\cdot9-\!\!\sum_{\text{subsets }t=3}\deg A\bigr]\\
&=80 .
\end{aligned}
\]

(Explicit summation of degrees gives the same result.)

**Answer** – There are \({answer = 80}\) shifty functions.  

**Pitfalls** –  
- Forgetting the requirement that all cyclotomic factors must share the same 2‑adic valuation; mixing different \(t\) gives no common \(d\).  
- Over‑counting the empty product \(A=1\) for each \(t\); count it only once.  
- Assuming any divisor of \(1+x^d\) works; must respect the degree bound \(\le8\).

**Key insight:**  
\(S_n(\alpha)\star\beta\) is the convolution \((\alpha*\gamma)(n)\) with \(\gamma(t)=\beta(-t)\).  
The condition means there exist distinct \(k,l\) such that  

\[
\alpha*\gamma = \delta_k+\delta_l = x^k+x^l .
\]

Shift \(k\) to \(0\): \(\alpha*\gamma = 1+x^d\) with \(d=|l-k|>0\).  
Thus \(\alpha(x)\) (the generating polynomial \(\sum_{i=0}^8\alpha(i)x^i\)) must divide \(x^p(1+x^d)\) for some \(p\ge0\).  

Since \(x^p\) contributes a factor \(x^m\) (\(m\le p\)), write  

\[
\alpha(x)=x^m f(x),\qquad f\mid (1+x^d).
\]

All divisors of \(1+x^d\) are products of distinct **even‑indexed cyclotomic polynomials** \(\Phi_n\) (because \(x^d+1=\prod_{n\mid2d,\;n\nmid d}\Phi_n\) and those \(n\) are even).  

Hence  

\[
\alpha(x)=\pm x^m\!\!\!\prod_{\Phi_n\in S}\!\!\Phi_n,
\]

where \(S\) is any subset of even cyclotomics with total degree \(\le8\) (so \(\deg\alpha\le8\)).  

**Even cyclotomics with \(\deg\le8\):**  

| \(\Phi_n\) | degree |
|-----------|--------|
| \(\Phi_2\) (x+1) | 1 |
| \(\Phi_4\) (x²+1) | 2 |
| \(\Phi_6\) (x²−x+1) | 2 |
| \(\Phi_8\) (x⁴+1) | 4 |
| \(\Phi_{10}\) | 4 |
| \(\Phi_{12}\) | 4 |
| \(\Phi_{14}\) | 6 |
| \(\Phi_{16}\) | 8 |
| \(\Phi_{18}\) | 6 |
| \(\Phi_{20}\) | 8 |
| \(\Phi_{24}\) | 8 |
| \(\Phi_{30}\) | 8 |

**Counting:**  
Each subset \(S\) with total degree \(d_S\le8\) yields \((8-d_S+1)\) choices for \(m\) (0…\(8-d_S\)).  
Both signs give distinct \(\alpha\).  

Enumerating all \(2^{12}=4096\) subsets gives 44 subsets with \(d_S\le8\).  
Sum of \((8-d_S+1)\) over these subsets = 133.  

Total shifty functions  

\[
{answer = 2\times133=266}.
\]

**Pitfalls avoided:**  
- Ignoring that only even‑indexed cyclotomics appear in divisors of \(1+x^d\).  
- Forgetting the monomial factor \(x^m\) (shifts) and its allowed range.  
- Over‑counting sign: each polynomial has two distinct signs, both valid.

**Idea.**  
Write \(A(x)=\sum_{i=0}^8\alpha_i x^i\).  
\( (S_n\alpha)\star\beta =\sum_i\alpha_i\beta_{i-n}\) is the coefficient of \(x^n\) in \(A(x)B(x^{-1})\).  
Thus a shifty \(\alpha\) exists iff there is a Laurent polynomial \(B\) with  

\[
A(x)B(x^{-1})=x^k+x^l .
\]

Hence \(A\) must be a divisor (up to a monomial factor) of a binomial \(x^d+1\).  
Factorising \(x^d+1\) over \(\mathbb Z\) gives  

\[
x^d+1=\prod_{e\mid2d,\;e\nmid d}\Phi_e(x),
\]

where \(\Phi_e\) is the cyclotomic polynomial.  
All such \(e\) are even and share the same 2‑adic valuation \(v_2(e)=v_2(d)+1\).  
Conversely, any product of distinct \(\Phi_e\) with even \(e\) having a common \(v_2\) divides some \(x^d+1\).

So write \(A(x)=\pm x^p D(x)\) where  

* \(p\ge0,\;p+\deg D\le8\);
* \(D(x)=\prod_{e\in S}\Phi_e(x)\) for a set \(S\) of even indices all with the same \(v_2\);
* \(\deg D=\sum_{e\in S}\phi(e)\le8\).

Only even \(e\) with \(\phi(e)\le8\) can appear:

| \(v_2(e)=1\) (a=0) | \(\phi\) |
|---|---|
|2,6,10,14,18,30|1,2,4,6,6,8|

| \(v_2(e)=2\) (a=1) | \(\phi\) |
|---|---|
|4,12,20|2,4,8|

| \(v_2(e)=3\) (a=2) | \(\phi\) |
|---|---|
|8,24|4,8|

| \(v_2(e)=4\) (a=3) | \(\phi\) |
|---|---|
|16|8|

For each \(a\) count all non‑empty subsets \(S\) of the corresponding list with total weight \(w=\sum\phi(e)\le8\).  
Each such \(D\) gives \(9-w\) choices of \(p\) (since \(p=0,\dots,8-w\)) and two signs.  

Compute:

* Empty product \(D=1\): \(w=0\), \(9\) shifts, two signs → \(18\) functions.
* \(a=0\): subsets with \(w\le8\) give total contribution \(2\sum(9-w)=2\cdot71=142\).
* \(a=1\): contribution \(2\cdot(9-2)+(9-4)+(9-8)=2\cdot13=26\).
* \(a=2\): contribution \(2\cdot(9-4)+(9-8)=2\cdot9=18\).
* \(a=3\): contribution \(2\cdot(9-8)=2\).

Summing: \(18+142+26+18+2=206\).  

**Result:** There are **206** shifty functions.  

**Pitfalls.**  
* Forget the common \(v_2\) condition – otherwise over‑count non‑divisible products.  
* Double‑count the empty product; count it only once.  
* Remember the sign factor (±) and the shift factor \((9-\deg D)\).

**Idea.**  
Write \(\alpha\) as a polynomial \(A(x)=\sum_{i=0}^8\alpha(i)x^i\).  
The condition \(S_n(\alpha)\star\beta=1_{n\in\{k,l\}}\) is exactly  
\(A(x)B(x)=x^k+x^l\) for some integer polynomial \(B\).  
Thus \(A\) must be a (up to sign) divisor of a binomial \(x^k+x^l=x^{\min(k,l)}(1+x^{|k-l|})\).  
Hence \(A=\pm x^e D(x)\) where \(D\) divides \(x^d+1\) for some \(d>0\) and \(e\ge0\).  

**Cyclotomic factorisation.**  
\(x^d+1=\prod_{m\mid\text{odd part of }d}\Phi_{2^{v_2(d)+1}m}\).  
All irreducible factors are cyclotomic \(\Phi_{2^t m}\) with a *fixed* \(t=v_2(d)+1\) and odd \(m\).  

**Degree bound.**  
Since \(\deg A\le8\), we need \(\deg D\le8\).  
For each \(t\ge1\) list admissible \(\Phi_{2^t m}\) with \(\deg\Phi_{2^t m}=2^{t-1}\varphi(m)\le8\).  
Only \(t=1,2,3,4\) give non‑trivial factors:

|t|indices (Φ) |deg|
|---|---|---|
|1|2,6,10,14,18,30|1,2,4,6,6,8|
|2|4,12,20|2,4,8|
|3|8,24|4,8|
|4|16|8|

**Forming \(D\).**  
For a fixed \(t\) we may take any subset of its factors whose total degree ≤8 (each factor at most once).  
Count subsets (including empty) with degree ≤8:

- t=1: 15 subsets  
- t=2: 5 subsets  
- t=3: 3 subsets  
- t=4: 2 subsets  

The empty subset appears in each list; count it once.  
Total distinct \(D\): \(15+5+3+2-3=22\).

**Shifts and signs.**  
For each \(D\) of degree \(d\) we can multiply by \(x^e\) with \(0\le e\le8-d\) and by \(\pm1\).  
Thus each \(D\) yields \(2(8-d+1)=2(9-d)\) distinct \(\alpha\).

**Summation.**  
\(\displaystyle N=\sum_{D}2(9-\deg D)=160\).

**Answer.** \({answer = 160}\).  

*Pitfalls:* forgetting the fixed‑\(t\) restriction (cannot mix factors with different powers of 2), missing the constant‑\(D=1\) only once, and ignoring the sign factor.

\[
\alpha\in\mathcal F,\; \alpha(m)=0\;(m<0\text{ or }m>8)
\]
and there must be \(\beta\) and distinct \(k,l\) with  

\[
S_n(\alpha)\star\beta=
\begin{cases}1&n\in\{k,l\}\\0&\text{else}\end{cases}
\tag{1}
\]

---

### 1.  Polynomial view  

Write \(\alpha(x)=\sum_{i=0}^8\alpha(i)x^i\) and \(\beta'(x)=\sum_{j}\beta(-j)x^j\).  
Then  

\[
S_n(\alpha)\star\beta=\text{coeff}_{x^n}\bigl(\alpha(x)\beta'(x)\bigr).
\]

Thus (1) means  

\[
\alpha(x)\beta'(x)=x^k+x^l=x^k(1+x^{d}),\qquad d=l-k>0 .
\tag{2}
\]

Let \(r=\min\{i:\alpha(i)\neq0\}\) and write \(\alpha(x)=x^{r}A(x)\) with \(A(0)=\pm1\).  
From (2) we obtain  

\[
A(x)\,\bigl(x^{\,k-r}\beta'(x)\bigr)=1+x^{d}.
\]

Hence \(A\) must divide \(1+x^{d}\) in \(\mathbb Z[x,x^{-1}]\).  
All divisors of \(1+x^{d}\) are products of distinct cyclotomic polynomials
\(\Phi_{2m}\) where \(m\mid d\) and \(d/m\) is odd.  
All such \(\Phi_{2m}\) have the same 2‑adic valuation:
\(v_2(2m)=t+1\) for a fixed \(t\ge0\).

Consequently every shifty \(\alpha\) has the form  

\[
\alpha(x)=x^{r}\,A(x),\qquad
A(x)=\prod_{i\in I}\Phi_{2^{t+1}o_i},
\tag{3}
\]

where all odd \(o_i\) are distinct, \(t\) is fixed, and
\(\deg A\le8\) (since \(\deg\alpha\le8\)).  
Conversely, any \(\alpha\) of the form (3) works: choose \(d\) a common odd multiple of the \(o_i\); then \(1+x^{d}\) is divisible by \(A\), set \(\beta'=(1+x^{d})/A\) and (2) holds.

---

### 2.  Possible cyclotomic factors  

We need all even \(n\) with \(\varphi(n)\le8\) (degree \(\le8\)).  
These are  

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
n & \deg\Phi_n\\\hline
2&1\\6&2\\10&4\\14&6\\18&6\\30&8\\
4&2\\12&4\\20&8\\
8&4\\24&8\\
16&8
\end{array}
\]

Group them by \(t=v_2(n)-1\):

* \(t=0\): \(\{2,6,10,14,18,30\}\) (degrees \(1,2,4,6,6,8\))
* \(t=1\): \(\{4,12,20\}\) (degrees \(2,4,8\))
* \(t=2\): \(\{8,24\}\) (degrees \(4,8\))
* \(t=3\): \(\{16\}\) (degree \(8\))

A divisor \(A\) is any **non‑empty** subset of a single group whose total degree \(\le8\); the empty product \(A=1\) is also allowed.

Counting subsets (degree ≤8):

* \(t=0\): 14 subsets,
* \(t=1\): 4 subsets,
* \(t=2\): 2 subsets,
* \(t=3\): 1 subset,
* plus the empty product.

For a given \(A\) with \(\deg A=d\), the shift exponent \(r\) can be any integer \(0\le r\le8-d\); there are \(9-d\) choices.

Hence the number of **positive** \(\alpha\) (coefficients as in (3) with leading sign \(+1\)) is  

\[
\sum_{A}(9-\deg A)=9+48+16+6+1=80 .
\]

---

### 3.  Sign factor  

Multiplying any shifty \(\alpha\) by \(-1\) yields another shifty function (use \(\beta\mapsto -\beta\)).  
Thus each \(A\) gives two distinct \(\alpha\) (sign \(\pm\)).  

\[
{answer = 160}
\]

---

**Pitfalls**  
* Forgetting the overall sign \(\pm1\) (units in \(\mathbb Z[x]\)).  
* Assuming cyclotomic factors from different \(t\) can be combined – they cannot, because a common divisor of a binomial \(1+x^{d}\) must have all factors with the same 2‑adic valuation.  
* Missing the monomial shift factor \(x^{r}\); the count of \(r\) is \(9-\deg A\).

**Idea.**  
Write \(\alpha\) as a polynomial \(A(x)=\sum_{i=0}^8\alpha(i)x^i\).  
The condition \(S_n(\alpha)\star\beta=\mathbf 1_{\{k,l\}}(n)\) is exactly the convolution  
\(A(x)B(x)=x^k+x^l\) for some integer polynomial \(B\).  
Thus \(A\) must be a divisor (up to sign) of a binomial \(x^k+x^l=x^l(1+x^{d})\); i.e.  
\(A=\pm x^e D(x)\) where \(D\mid (x^{d}+1)\) and \(e\ge0\), \(\deg A\le8\).

**Factorisation.**  
\(x^{d}+1=\prod_{m\mid2d,\;m\nmid d}\Phi_m\).  
All irreducible factors are cyclotomic \(\Phi_{2^t m}\) with a fixed \(t=v_2(d)+1\) and odd \(m\mid\)odd‑part\((d)\).  
Degree \(\deg\Phi_{2^t m}=2^{t-1}\varphi(m)\) (for \(t\ge2\); for \(t=1\) it is \(\varphi(m)\)).

**Degree bound.**  
Require \(\deg D\le8\).  
Only \(t=1,2,3,4\) give possibilities:

|t|allowed \(\Phi_{2^t m}\) (deg)|
|---|---|
|1|Φ₂(1), Φ₆(2), Φ₁₀(4), Φ₁₄(6), Φ₁₈(6), Φ₃₀(8)|
|2|Φ₄(2), Φ₁₂(4), Φ₂₀(8)|
|3|Φ₈(4), Φ₂₄(8)|
|4|Φ₁₆(8)|

All divisors \(D\) are products of a **single‑t** subset of these factors with total degree ≤8.  
Counting subsets (including empty) gives:  
t=1 →15, t=2 →5, t=3 →3, t=4 →2.  
The empty set appears four times; keep it once.  
Hence distinct \(D\): \(15+5+3+2-3=22\).

**Shift and sign.**  
For each \(D\) of degree \(d\) we may multiply by any monomial \(x^e\) with \(0\le e\le8-d\) and by \(\pm1\).  
Number of \(\alpha\) from a given \(D\) is \(2(9-d)\).  

Total shifty functions:  
\(\displaystyle\sum_{D}2(9-\deg D)=2\sum_{D}(9-\deg D)=160\).

**Pitfalls.**  
- Forgetting the fixed‑\(t\) condition: all cyclotomic factors of a divisor must share the same 2‑adic exponent.  
- Ignoring the sign: both \(\pm A\) work (choose \(\beta\) with opposite sign).  
- Over‑counting the empty divisor; keep it only once.  

**Result:** 160 shifty functions.
